title: The Wolf and the Goat
summary: A wolf, pacing hungrily along the base of a towering limestone cliff, looked up and spotted a goat grazing peacefully upon a high, narrow ledge where the grass grew sweet among the rocks. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that beware the friendly advice of an enemy who seeks only your downfall.
full_text: A wolf, pacing hungrily along the base of a towering limestone cliff, looked up and spotted a goat grazing peacefully upon a high, narrow ledge where the grass grew sweet among the rocks. The cliff was so sheer and precipitous that no wolf could possibly climb its face without breaking his neck. Licking his lips, the wolf called out in a warm, friendly voice filled with apparent concern: "Good neighbor! Why do you risk your life upon that terrifying, dizzying ledge where one false step could send you plummeting to your death? Come down to this lush, green meadow below! The grass here is far sweeter, the water is cool, and you can graze in safety and comfort!" The goat paused in her chewing, looked down over the cliff edge, and replied with calm mockery: "I thank you for your kind concern, neighbor Wolf! But you are not inviting me down because the grass here is scarce, or because you care for my safety. You are inviting me down because you are starving, and your appetite is keen for my meat, not my well-being!"
moral: Beware the friendly advice of an enemy who seeks only your downfall.

quiz.question: What essential truth does "The Wolf and the Goat" teach young readers?
options: Beware the friendly advice of an enemy who seeks only your downfall.
Might and physical strength always triumph over truth and wisdom
